body: [{"streamId":"01a0de52-d8a3-739c-81d9-f4b65aebca52","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0de52-d8a3-739c-81d9-f4b65aebca52\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a0a27f-abdf-7731-84aa-d604e9bc53ca\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022The README becomes a short, high-level front page (what odo is, why it exists, features, a quick start, a docs index) and every detail it holds today moves into a docs/ directory organized by topic, rewritten in Brian\\u0027s own voice with every fact preserved and the history split out into a dated decisions file\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022README.md is at most about 400 words and holds exactly six parts in this order: what it is (the current two-sentence pitch and the one question it answers); why it exists (objective and benefits in one paragraph, no bulleted benefits list); features (six to eight bullets, each a phrase linking to its docs file); quick start (clone, dotnet build, set the two listing keys with dotnet user-secrets, run odo search, then a link to docs/running.md; the agent proves it by cloning the branch into a temp directory and running dotnet build and the help command there); docs (one line per docs/ file); status (one sentence: v0, one purchase, one scenario, built for one person, no releases). Nothing in the README explains a mechanism; that all lives in docs/\u0022,\u0022docs/ holds these files with these contents: setup.md (the .NET SDK, clone and build, the three secrets and their environment variables, the data directory per platform and ODO_DATA_DIR, the browser the walk and dealer grade attach to with a pointer to walk.md, and the former Development section: build and test lines, 80-column tables, NO_COLOR); running.md (a run start to finish as seven numbered steps in this order: search, walk, research, dealer grade, budget, rank, show, then note and finalist, one or two sentences each on what you get, ending with the statement that everything is run by hand and nothing is scheduled, and that search and walk are worth rerunning whenever a fresh picture of the market is wanted, with research, grading, and rank after them); commands.md (the table reordered into that run order, one line per command with its flags and a short phrase, followed by a section per command holding the flag explanations, and a Search section holding the two APIs, the used-cars-only rule, the placeholder-price rule, and the five diff headings shared with walk); research.md (five subsections: what is fetched, caching and refresh with the NHTSA error note as one sentence, running odo research with the progress and tally lines, red flags opened by one table with a row per kind giving tag, rule, and threshold and followed by one short paragraph per flag for its exceptions with the seller-group clustering explained once, and how rank and show display research status); walk.md (six subsections: your browser with all six launch lines kept, leave the window open, and the bot-challenge pause; what a walk does, covering site and model order, the cap and what does and does not count against it, pacing, background tabs, continuing past a failed pair, the per-pair line, the end table, and the diff headings with the Gone reasons; rules every site shares, covering scenario facets, the hybrid-only-from-year rule, the wrong-model check with the title backstop, and the new-car drop; per site with a short subsection each for cars.com, Carvana, and Autotrader; recorded pages, where they land and how files are named; extraction, the claude CLI versus an API key, what the prompt asks for, and how nulls are treated, moved here from the secrets section); dealers.md (how a dealer is identified, the Carvana and Private seller rows that are never looked up, the grade pass split into what it looks up, how a card is matched, and what counts as checked, and where grades appear in rank and show); cost-model.md (what a purchase price means, the three monthly figures and how each is built, and where they appear: budget\\u0027s maximum purchase price per target, rank\\u0027s during-loan and ten-year columns and its unmet-target notice, and show\\u0027s itemized block with the rounding reconciliation); scenario.md (the scenario file field by field, the per-model maps including hybridOnlyFromModelYear and minModelYearOverrides, and how to pass a different scenario); ledger.md (a page at most: each table, vehicles, postings, price observations, runs, dealers, and VIN records, what one row means, how a run stamps LastSeen, and the SQLite location); decisions.md (dated entries, one per reversal or worked example the current README tells as history: the hybrid facet misread from the spike recording and Brian\\u0027s pasted URLs, the CarEdge search URL move, the two-search Camry rule, the seller-group clustering motivated by the sixteen-rooftop syndicated Camry, the same-dealer mileage-drop softening, and any other story the agent lifts out; the research and walk docs keep only the rule); spike-findings.md (the current SPIKE-FINDINGS.md moved with git mv, links to it fixed, content unchanged)\u0022,\u0022Every fact in the current README appears exactly once in the new set and no fact is invented: the pull request description carries a table mapping each current README section to its new home, and lists every sentence that was dropped with a one-line reason; every class name, flag, file path, URL parameter, and threshold in the new docs is checked against the code on the branch as it stands after the cap tasks (726ebd91, 238da0a2, 5bdae3aa) merged, since those change the walk\\u0027s cap, paging, and known-card behavior and their README hunks must be carried into walk.md\u0022,\u0022Everything is written in Brian\\u0027s voice using the my-voice skill: load the skill if the session offers it, otherwise read /Users/brianhallmanac/.claude/skills/my-voice/SKILL.md and /Users/brianhallmanac/.claude/skills/my-voice/contexts/explainer.md directly and follow them; complete flowing sentences of about seventeen words, contractions, plain words, cause and effect over feature lists, paragraphs of two to four sentences and never more than about 150 words, headers only where a reader needs to navigate, bullets only to enumerate; plus the house conventions: no em dashes, full sentences, no AI attribution anywhere\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings (no code changes are expected; a docs-only diff); the run skill file in the project home is not touched; commits are small with conventional messages: one commit that moves SPIKE-FINDINGS.md, one per new docs file or coherent group, and one that cuts the README down last so every intermediate commit still has a complete README\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Chore\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Walked with Brian in the orchestrator window on 2026-09-26 from about 08:50 to 11:40 EDT; the full rulings, stop by stop, are in /Users/brianhallmanac/.hall9k/projects/odonomics/notes/readme-walk-2026-09-26.md and the criteria above restate them. Brian\\u0027s framing, in his words: \\u0027the README itself should be very short and concise, and at a high level, about what this app does, features, benefits, that kind of thing. From there, it dives into docs.\\u0027 He rejected a GitHub wiki because it is not part of the repo. The current README is about 7,300 words and accurate through every merged PR; its problem is shape, not staleness: three walk paragraphs of 378, 464, and 1,030 words written as a decision log (what an earlier build believed, what the spike recorded, what Brian pasted from Edge), a research section of 1,900 words with no subheadings whose mileage-drop bullet alone runs 650 words, and a dealer-grades section whose first 500 words are about dealer identity rather than grading. Section word counts at the walk: intro and setup 355, commands 507, research 1,869, walk 2,595, dealer grades 1,171, costs and scenario 1,022, development 44. There are no releases, tags, or workflows; it is clone, build, set keys, run, and dotnet publish yields a local odo executable rather than a release. This task is blocked on 5bdae3aa so that the three cap tasks\\u0027 README hunks exist before the split; read their merged diffs to README.md first. The five diff headings after search and walk are New, Also listed at, Moved, Price drops, and Gone (PR #47). The existing README paragraph order is the source of truth for facts; when the new organization makes two old sentences say the same thing, keep one. Do not touch the run skill file in the project home; the orchestrator updates
